article.title: JDK 28's Project Page Lists Ten JEPs Targeted So Far: Value Objects in Preview, Structured Concurrency Finalized, Rampdown Phase One on December 3
article.summary: OpenJDK's JDK 28 page lists ten JEPs targeted so far; seven show Integrated on their pages. Two Valhalla JEPs are in preview and InfoQ reports Structured Concurrency is final. JDK 27 had five preview or incubator JEPs among nine.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

OpenJDK's [JDK 28 project page](https://openjdk.org/projects/jdk/28/), last updated 2026/11/2 14:47 UTC, lists ten JEPs under the heading "JEPs targeted to JDK 28, so far." The same page schedules Rampdown Phase One, the branch from the main line, for 2026/12/03 and general availability for 2027/03/09. By the Herald's own tally of the ten JEP pages as fetched on 2026-11-09, seven show the status Integrated, one Completed, one "Closed / Delivered" and one, JEP 535, Targeted. The list includes the two JEPs that InfoWorld's Simon Ritter describes as the first real parts of Project Valhalla, both in preview, and a Structured Concurrency API that [InfoQ reports](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/10/jep-543-jdk-28/) has reached final status. This analysis sets that list against JDK 27's, using the OpenJDK pages, the OpenJDK source commits and reporting by InfoQ and InfoWorld.

## Background: JDK 27 and a long preview cycle

[JDK 27](https://openjdk.org/projects/jdk/27/) reached general availability on 15 September 2026 with nine JEPs. Five of them carry a preview or incubator label in their titles on that page: Lazy Constants (Third Preview), Primitive Types in Patterns, instanceof, and switch (Fifth Preview), Structured Concurrency (Seventh Preview), Vector API (Twelfth Incubator) and PEM Encodings of Cryptographic Objects (Third Preview). Simon Ritter, who is identified as the Deputy CTO of Azul, wrote in [InfoWorld's New Tech Forum](https://www.infoworld.com/article/4229750/jdk-27-the-quiet-before-the-storm.html) that "In JDK 27, we have nine JEPs, and five of them are features that continue to be revised under the preview feature and incubator modules concept." He summarized the release as bringing "mostly incremental changes to preview features" and wrote that the Vector API authors do not want to finalize it until Valhalla is delivered.

The longest of those cycles is Structured Concurrency. According to [JEP 543](https://openjdk.org/jeps/543), it was first delivered as an incubator module via JEP 428 (JDK 19) and JEP 437 (JDK 20), became a preview API via JEP 453 (JDK 21), and re-previewed through JEP 533 in JDK 27. InfoQ describes its finalization as concluding "the longest preview cycle of any Project Loom feature." The PEM API followed a shorter path: [JEP 542](https://openjdk.org/jeps/542) records a first preview via JEP 470 (JDK 25), a second via JEP 524 (JDK 26) and a third via JEP 538 (JDK 27), and proposes to finalize the API "without further change."

## Current situation: what the ten JEPs are

The following grouping and the counts in it are the Herald's own, built from the JEP pages and the project page as fetched on 2026-11-09. Commit times are the committer timestamps of the implementing commits in the [openjdk/jdk repository](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk), in UTC.

**Preview and incubator (three of ten, counted from the titles on the project page).**

- JEP 401, Value Objects (Preview), and JEP 539, Strict Field Initialization in the JVM (Preview), were implemented in [one commit](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/commit/cc278dbb8a1ca0754d5842708b9029441055d361) whose message names both, committed at 2026-07-31 00:45:12 UTC. Ritter called them "the first real parts of Project Valhalla." [JEP 401](https://openjdk.org/jeps/401) says 30 classes in the Java Platform API are now declared value classes, among them Integer, Long, Optional, LocalDate and Duration. [JEP 539](https://openjdk.org/jeps/539) describes itself as a preview VM feature "available for use by compilers that emit class files."
- [JEP 540](https://openjdk.org/jeps/540), Simple JSON API (Incubator), was implemented in a [commit](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/commit/39f3ef1b97917110e5237ad2bbe4f6bcec1bd5e5) at 2026-09-09 16:45:40 UTC. The Herald covered its targeting in an [earlier article](/article/2026-08/19-openjdk-targets-jep-540-for-jdk-28-giving-java-a-built-in-json-api-for-the-first-time).

**Without a preview or incubator label.**

- JEP 543, Structured Concurrency, was implemented in a [commit](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/commit/cd37d2bb07b7a050b4925ed3312c2a8dd7a801b1) at 2026-10-17 06:06:44 UTC. InfoQ's article of October 19, 2026 says it was integrated into JDK 28, bringing the API to final status "with no API changes from JDK 27's seventh preview."
- JEP 542, PEM Encodings of Cryptographic Objects, shows the status Completed on its page.
- [JEP 544](https://openjdk.org/jeps/544), Ahead-of-Time Code Compilation, was implemented in a [commit](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/commit/f6fa65381d0c32e22120159415f8c472e990cdc7) at 2026-10-08 21:31:21 UTC. The JEP's own measurements, run on a recent JDK 28 early-access build with five framework-based benchmark applications on a two-core Linux/x64 system, report startup-time reductions of around 50% to 70% from the AOT cache alone and around 65% to 80% with AOT code. These are the JEP authors' figures, not independent ones.
- [JEP 545](https://openjdk.org/jeps/545), Faster Startup and Warmup with ZGC, and [JEP 546](https://openjdk.org/jeps/546), Adaptive Heap Sizing for ZGC, were implemented together in one [commit](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/commit/d544fca92aab371187df86fbbf3b473abdab25b2) at 2026-10-21 14:09:08 UTC. JEP 545's motivation section says that with ZGC today the JVM "starts up in about a tenth of a second with a 2MB initial heap but requires over ten seconds with a 32GB initial heap."
- [JEP 535](https://openjdk.org/jeps/535), Shenandoah GC: Generational Mode by Default, shows the status Targeted, not Integrated. It would switch the default mode to generational and deprecate the non-generational mode.
- [JEP 541](https://openjdk.org/jeps/541), Deprecate the macOS/x64 Port for Removal, shows "Closed / Delivered"; its implementing [commit](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/commit/ee2ebf6bd75bac05f4446a2cacd0a2f5e7d9c45c) is dated 2026-08-27 21:01:38 UTC. An [earlier Herald article](/article/2026-11/05-intel-macs-and-developer-tooling-jdk-homebrew-and-a-nodejs-alpha-lower-macos-x64-support-on-separate-timelines-as-macos-27-ends-intel-support) compares how JEP 541, Homebrew and a Node.js alpha lower macOS x64 support.

**How the list grew.** InfoWorld reported on September 24, 2026 that [AOT code compilation had been proposed](https://www.infoworld.com/article/4205791/java-28-starts-to-take-shape.html) for JDK 28, which it described as due in March 2027. InfoQ's Java News Roundup for the week of [September 28](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/10/java-news-roundup-sep28-2026/) says JEP 544 was "elevated from Proposed to Target to Targeted." The roundup for the week of [October 5](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/10/java-news-roundup-oct05-2026/) puts JEPs 543, 545 and 546 in the proposed-to-target stage, and the one for the week of [October 12](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/10/java-news-roundup-oct12-2026/) reports all three as targeted. Ritter's article, dated October 5, says "At the time of writing, there are six JEPs targeted," without naming all six; the project page now lists ten.

## Implications as the sources describe them

**Structured Concurrency.** InfoQ says that for codebases already on JDK 27 the migration "comes down to recompiling without --enable-preview," while teams coming from JDK 26 "will see FailedException replaced by ExecutionException and R_X added to custom joiner signatures." It adds that the API does not say which failure `join()` reports if several subtasks fail at once.

**Value objects.** JEP 401 says value objects are a preview language and VM feature, disabled by default; its instructions are to compile with `javac --release 28 --enable-preview` and run with `java --enable-preview`, with variants for the source launcher and jshell. Some platform classes "become value classes only when preview features are enabled; otherwise, they behave just as they did in JDK 27." The JEP states that the `==` operator compares value objects by their field values, and that synchronization is among the identity-sensitive operations value objects do not support: its jshell example shows an "unexpected type" error for a variable typed LocalDate and an IdentityException at run time when the reference is typed as Object.

**Fewer previews, by one measure.** By the Herald's count, three of JDK 28's ten titles carry a preview or incubator label, against five of nine in JDK 27, a count that matches Ritter's. Two of JDK 27's five preview JEPs, 533 and 538, reappear on the JDK 28 page as JEPs 543 and 542, whose histories cite them. The project page lists no JEP that continues JEP 532 or JEP 537, the Primitive Types and Vector API JEPs. [JEP 547](https://openjdk.org/jeps/547), Lazy Constants (Fourth Preview), has the status Candidate on its page and is not on the list.

**Framing.** Ritter titled his piece "JDK 27: The quiet before the storm" and said he would wait until JDK 28 is ready for release before discussing the Valhalla JEPs in detail.

## What We Don't Know

- None of the cited sources says whether JEP 535 will be integrated before Rampdown Phase One on 2026/12/03, or whether further JEPs will be added; the project page's own heading says the list is "so far."
- None of the cited sources states in which release value objects will leave preview.
- The figures in JEP 544 were measured by the JEP's authors on an early-access build; the cited sources include no independent measurement of them.
- The commit dates show when changes entered the main line, not when each feature will be stable in a release.
